subsystems.name: Core Compiler Runtime
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the entire jq-language front end and runtime: it scans and parses filter source, compiles it into a bytecode program, and executes that program against a stream of JSON values. It is split from the JSON value system so that language processing (parsing, binding, optimization, and VM interpretation) can evolve independently of the memory-managed `jv` data model and so both sides can be tested separately. Control flows from the flex-based scanner in `src/lexer.c` into the bison grammar in `src/parser.c`, whose `jq_parse` (`src/parser.c:4152`) returns a `block` tree; `compile` (`src/compile.c:1218`) then binds names and emits bytecode. At run time `jq_next` (`src/execute.c:340`) drives the interpreter loop, using the stack helpers in `src/exec_stack.h` and calling C builtins registered by `builtins_bind` (`src/builtin.c:2144`). Bytecode disassembly and deallocation live in `src/bytecode.c`, module/import resolution in `src/linker.c`, and source-location tracking in `src/locfile.c`. This subsystem connects to the JSON Value System through the `jv.h`/`jv.c` APIs used throughout `builtin.c` and `execute.c`, and to the command-line driver through `src/main.c` and `src/util.c`, which provide the program text and input values.

subsystems.name: JSON Value System
subsystems.description: This subsystem implements jq's JSON data model and all value I/O: reference-counted JSON values (`jv`), parsing, printing, number formatting, Unicode validation, and the CLI/test harness around them. It exists separately so the compiler/runtime can manipulate a stable value abstraction while all representation concerns (copy-on-write, allocation failure, decimal conversion, UTF-8, and output formatting) remain encapsulated in one place. Input data enters through `src/util.c`'s `jq_util_input_next_input` (`src/util.c:399`) and `main` (`src/main.c:289`), is converted by `jv_parse` (`src/jv_parse.c:913`) into a `jv`, and is printed by `jv_dump_term` (`src/jv_print.c:219`). Values are allocated with `jv_mem_alloc` (`src/jv_alloc.c:141`) and released by `jv_free` (`src/jv.c:2014`), while `jv_aux.c` supplies structural operations such as `jv_get`, `jv_set`, and `jv_setpath` used by the runtime. Floating-point rendering is delegated to `jvp_dtoa_fmt` (`src/jv_dtoa.c:4205`) and Unicode handling to `jvp_utf8_next` (`src/jv_unicode.c:30`). Tests in `jq_test.c` exercise both the value layer and the runtime, and the subsystem connects to Core Compiler Runtime through `execute.c`, `compile.c`, and `linker.c`, which call into these jv APIs.

subsystems.name: Decimal Number Library
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the vendor-supplied decNumber library, which provides arbitrary-precision decimal numbers and the three IEEE 754 decimal floating-point encodings (decimal32, decimal64, and decimal128) that jq uses to avoid binary floating-point artifacts in JSON numbers. It is kept as a separate vendored unit because it is a self-contained, externally maintained arithmetic package with its own headers, examples, and internal build assumptions; isolating it lets jq's own code treat decimal conversion as a stable interface. Text and numbers enter through `decNumberFromString` (`vendor/decNumber/decNumber.c:478`) and are converted to and from the dense packed decimal (DPD) storage formats by `decimal128FromNumber` (`vendor/decNumber/decimal128.c:74`) and `decimal64FromNumber` (`vendor/decNumber/decimal64.c:80`). Arithmetic and comparison operations such as `decExpOp` (`vendor/decNumber/decNumber.c:5227`) and `decCompareOp` (`vendor/decNumber/decNumber.c:6004`) operate on the generic `decNumber` type, while `decPackedToNumber` (`vendor/decNumber/decPacked.c:147`) and `decPackedFromNumber` (`vendor/decNumber/decPacked.c:59`) handle packed BCD exchange format. The existing `decNumber` type covers the Number Library role, while related `decContext.c`, `decDouble.c`, `decQuad.c`, and `decSingle.c` files are the parallel decimal core with which it shares design.

subsystems.name: Decimal Core Arithmetic
subsystems.description: This subsystem is the IEEE 754 decimal floating-point core of the vendored decNumber library, providing the common `decFloat` arithmetic engine shared by decSingle, decDouble, and decQuad. It is separated from the generic `decNumber` library because decimal floating point has a different representation (DPD-encoded fields) and a different operation set; decBasic.c and decCommon.c implement that DFP layer once instead of duplicating it for each format. Context and status flow through `decContextDefault` (`vendor/decNumber/decContext.c:72`) and `decContextTestStatus` (`vendor/decNumber/decContext.c:421`), which configure rounding and report exceptions for all arithmetic. Conversions enter through `decFloatFromString` (`vendor/decNumber/decCommon.c:776`) and leave through `decFloatToString` (`vendor/decNumber/decCommon.c:1500`), while `decFloatAdd` (`vendor/decNumber/decBasic.c:1102`), `decFiniteMultiply` (`vendor/decNumber/decBasic.c:708`), and `decDivide` (`vendor/decNumber/decBasic.c:167`) perform the core operations. Format-specific macros in `decDouble.c`, `decQuad.c`, and `decSingle.c` instantiate the public API, and the DPD conversion tables in `decDPD.h` feed the encoding helpers. It connects to the Number Library through `decNumber.h` and `decNumberLocal.h` conventions and to `decimal64.c`/`example8.c` in its related files, which use the same context and conversion functions.

subsystems.name: UTF-8 Table Generation
subsystems.description: This subsystem is a small build-time Python generator that emits static UTF-8 lookup tables for the C runtime. It exists as a separate script so the generated table data in `src/jv_utf8_tables.h` is produced reproducibly from Unicode definitions and is never hand-maintained inside the JSON value system. The top-level `table` constant and `mask` constant define the source data, `print_table` (`scripts/gen_utf8_tables.py:8`) writes a table in C syntax, and `utf8info` (`scripts/gen_utf8_tables.py:16`) computes the per-codepoint metadata that fills it. Although its `related_files` list is empty, the script's output is consumed by `src/jv_unicode.c` through `src/jv_utf8_tables.h` in the JSON Value System, so this is effectively a companion generation step for that subsystem.

files.role: Python script that generates the static UTF-8 tables included by the C code. It is invoked at build/development time, not at jq runtime.

overview.description: This is the jq codebase: a JSON processor with a custom filter language and a memory-managed JSON data model. The Core Compiler Runtime scans, parses, compiles, and interprets jq filters, while the JSON Value System provides the reference-counted jv values and JSON parsing/printing that the runtime consumes. The vendored Decimal Number Library and Decimal Core Arithmetic subsystems supply arbitrary-precision and decimal floating-point arithmetic for JSON number handling. The UTF-8 Table Generation script produces static Unicode lookup tables used by the JSON Value System, and an Error Injection Testing subsystem is included as a separate test component.
